data.label: Synthetic user (browser)
data.description: Synthetic test users chat through a browser. This is a client reference and is not provisioned.

data.label: Identity Platform
data.description: Signs in synthetic users and issues ID tokens. Cloud Run verifies each token, and the user ID in the token decides which conversations the user can access.

data.label: Assistant app (Cloud Run)
data.description: Serves the chat UI and API. It rejects requests without a valid token. Its internal modules build bounded context (a maximum number of turns and bytes, plus a maximum output token count), give a recoverable fallback reply with retry if the model fails or times out, delete conversations on request, and publish an approved context snapshot for escalation. It takes no external actions.

data.label: Conversation store (Firestore)
data.description: Stores conversations under users/{uid}/conversations. Only the Cloud Run service account can access the store, and the app filters every query by the verified user ID. Deleting a conversation removes the conversation and its messages.

data.label: Gemini on Vertex AI
data.description: Model runtime that the app calls with its service account. The model version, regional availability and quota are not verified yet. The local test replaces this with a scripted mock.

data.label: Escalation topic (Pub/Sub)
data.description: Carries escalation events that hold the approved conversation context snapshot. Delivery is at least once, so events carry an idempotency key, and a dead-letter topic is planned.

data.label: Human support reviewer
data.description: Person who receives escalated conversations. The handling tool for this person is not decided yet.

data.label: Cloud Logging & Monitoring
data.description: Records request, denial, model-error and escalation metrics and sends alerts. Logs must not contain the content of conversations.

brief.application: Use Google Cloud for this synthetic architecture qualification. Build an authenticated conversational assistant for synthetic users. Include an application, per-user conversation state, model runtime, bounded context and an escalation path. No external actions in this first test. Acceptance criteria: One user cannot read another conversation; Context and response sizes are bounded; Model outage produces a recoverable response; Deleting a conversation removes its stored context; Escalation retains the approved conversation context. Draw the complete end-to-end architecture with concrete service choices and connected flows. Explain the first local test, distinguish mocked model behavior from actual model validation, and ask one useful missing-decision question. Do not reduce this application to storage to satisfy generator coverage. Do not invent successful deployment or approved region/account access.

lastAsked.question: What information will it work with, and where does it live?
lastAsked.beginner: For example a database, documents, or another system's data.
lastAsked.why: It shapes the AI architecture design.

requirements.statement: A user can read, list or delete only their own conversations, and a request for another user's conversation is denied.
requirements.rationale: If conversation data leaks between users, the isolation guarantee is broken.
requirements.basis: User acceptance criterion: One user cannot read another conversation.

requirements.statement: The prompt context and the model response each have a configured maximum size. Requests above the limit are trimmed or rejected.
requirements.rationale: Size limits control cost, delay and how much data is exposed.
requirements.basis: User acceptance criterion: Context and response sizes are bounded.

requirements.statement: If the model times out or fails, the user gets a recoverable reply and the conversation is kept.
requirements.rationale: Model failures must not lose conversation state or end the session.
requirements.basis: User acceptance criterion: Model outage produces a recoverable response.

requirements.statement: Deleting a conversation removes its stored context and messages.
requirements.rationale: Stored context must not remain after a user deletes a conversation.
requirements.basis: User acceptance criterion: Deleting a conversation removes its stored context.

requirements.statement: An escalation sends the approved conversation context to a human reviewer and keeps it available to that reviewer.
requirements.rationale: Without the context, the reviewer cannot continue the case.
requirements.basis: User acceptance criterion: Escalation retains the approved conversation context.

decisions.title: Authenticated conversational assistant on Google Cloud (first sketch)
decisions.context: Scope: an authenticated chat assistant for synthetic users with per-user conversation state, a Vertex AI model runtime, bounded context and a human escalation path. It takes no external actions. Assumptions: the region is not selected yet; Gemini model access, quotas and regional availability have not been verified; the graph shows intended design only and does not prove access rules, deployment or model quality. Native Terraform generation for this workload is not available yet, so engineering is still required.
